text:
alex: heads up — our synthetic streaming probe for embeddings in us-west1 is spiking 'unhealthy' for the last ~45m. lots of TLS handshake failures and intermittent 502s. p95 latency jumped to ~1.2s earlier. seen from two independent probe runners. grafana panel attached (streaming-errors > threshold).
sre-bot: Alert fired: blackbox/streaming-us-west1 — error_rate(5m) > 3% (8 matches)
maya: is this related to the cert rotation we did last night?
chris: certs look fine on the control plane. sampled logs show lots of "tls: handshake did not complete" and some "connection reset by peer" from envoy sidecars on inference-pool-usw1. correlates with a node pool rolling update around 02:10 UTC.
ian: can you paste the prometheus query you used? want to see if it's a single probe or aggregate noise.
alex: query I used: `sum by (job, region) (rate(blackbox_exporter_probe_failed_total{job="blackbox", probe_type="streaming"}[5m])) / sum by (job, region) (rate(blackbox_exporter_probe_total{job="blackbox", probe_type="streaming"}[5m]))` — shows spike across multiple runners in us-west1.
taylor: sounds like a transient infra flake from the rolling pool. two things: (1) tune the alert to avoid firing on short rolling windows, (2) reduce probe aggression so we don't DDOS the LB during reconverge.
chris: agreed. also noticed probes target the general inference LB; can we tag some probes to hit canary-gpu-pool instead? that would reduce noise to production routes.
maya: cost note — synthetic streaming probes are expensive because they keep the stream open and incur egress + model token units. we currently run ~600 streaming probes/s across regions during business hours. if we sample more aggressively when traffic is low we can save credits.
alex: pushed a quick config suggestion to our internal gist. plan: bump probe timeout from 3s -> 6s, add interval jitter, and add a probe label to hit canary pool for embeddings. snippet: ```yaml
blackbox_probes:
  - name: streaming-embed-usw1
    type: streaming
    target: https://inference-usw1.internal/redwood/embeddings
    labels:
      region: us-west1
      probe_pool: canary
    interval: 10s
    jitter: 10%
    timeout: 6s
    sample_rate: 0.25  # only 25% of previous runners during off-peak
```
ian: for alerts: change from firing on any probe error to: `increase(blackbox_exporter_probe_failed_total{probe_type="streaming"}[10m]) > 10` grouped by region+model. plus a for: 5m in alertmanager to reduce flapping. I'll open a PR for the rule and update the grafana panel to split streaming vs unary.
taylor: also add silence window during planned rolling updates or when nodepool autoscaler is reconciling. we can auto-silence via the deploybot tag into alertmanager.
chris: small infra ask — can we set k8s anti-affinity on probe runners so they don't all land on nodes being drained during a rolling update? reduces correlated failures.
maya: agree, and add a runbook line: if handshake errors spike during nodepool updates, treat as infra drain, escalate only if errors persist >20m and affect >= 3 AZs.
ian: I'll open three PRs: (1) alertmanager rule change, (2) probe config with sampling & canary label, (3) grafana dashboard split + runbook link. tagging oncall now — please silence while we roll.
sre-bot: Alert silenced: blackbox/streaming-us-west1 for 30m by ian
alex: LGTM. after PRs merge we'll watch for regressions. if we still see TLS handshakes, we'll capture tcpdump from envoy and open a support ticket with cloud-net.
taylor: thanks all. updating the incident channel with concise summary and cost impact estimate once ian's PRs are in.
chris: quick reminder — when we sample streaming probes, ensure we still keep an absolute minimum of N probes per availability zone to catch region-wide issues.
maya: noted. i'll add that to the config template (min_per_az: 3).
ian: done for now, fingers crossed. will follow up in the dashboard PR.
